text:
Juniper: quick architecture follow-up — during mixed workloads we saw increased tail when prefetch ran before demote bookkeeping completed. wondering if ordering is wrong (prefetch triggered on stale mark before demote finalizes).

Marco: saw that on canary. flow looks like: request touches page -> mark stale -> worker spawns prefetch sync -> demote later tries to reclaim but race means prefetch writes back more pages than necessary.

Sofia: tradeoffs: delaying prefetch until demote confirms reduces redundant IO but may increase miss latency for the current request. alternative: let prefetch start but make it cancelable if demote compacts the page set.

Juniper: cancelable prefetch seems promising. Implementation idea: assign a short-lived prefetch token with a generation id; demote increments generation and any in-flight prefetch with older gen is dropped. avoids wasted writes.

Marco: nice. need to ensure cancellation doesn't leak NVMe IOs mid-flight — only cancel before submission to IO queue. once queued, let it finish.

Sofia: also think about affinity: prefetch and coalesce currently run on shared background pool and steal cycles from infer tasks occasionally. propose background workers use sched_affinity group "background" and a runtime admission gate that checks current request latency EWMA before scheduling heavy coalesce.

Juniper: config sketch:
```
prefetch:
  cancelable: true
  cancel_gen_window_ms: 4
  max_sync_prefetch_pages: 4
background:
  cpu_group: background
  latency_ewma_threshold_ms: 6
```

Marco: observability: prefetch_cancel_count, prefetch_dropped_before_io, demote_compaction_savings_bytes. will add pool+tenant tags.

sre-bot: alert rule created: prefetch_dropped_before_io > 1000 in 5m -> paging-team paging-alerts.

Sofia: one more subtlety: when we cancel prefetch we must leave page state consistent for next touch; ensure we roll back any temporary metadata (prefetch_inflight flag).

Juniper: agreed. I'll draft RFC follow-up and a microbenchmark to show bytes saved vs extra miss latency. planning a canary after tests.

Marco: I'll add the token-gen bits to the prefetch path and a fast check before IO submit.

Sofia: will prepare canary job and rollback thresholds.

Juniper: thanks — closing thread, PR link incoming.
